root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Neo-Orthodox Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 d5 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Rc1

overview: White has pinned the f6 knight and moved the rook to c1 (the Anti-Neo-Orthodox line), and Black usually plays ...h6 7.Bh4 b6 and then trades with ...Nxd5 and ...exd5 after cxd5. This leads to a Carlsbad-like structure where White plays for a minority attack and Black for solid defence with ...c5 or ...Bb7. The line is mostly quiet and very solid for Black.

white_ideas.idea: Pin on f6, then cxd5 and Bxe7, and play the minority attack with b4-b5.
Use the c-file with Rc1 and pressure on c6/c5.

black_ideas.idea: Challenge the pin with ...h6 and ...b6 and trade pieces on d5 and e7 to ease the position.
Hold d5, develop ...Bb7 and play ...c5 or ...c6 to free the c8-bishop.

typical_structures.structure: Carlsbad structure after cxd5 exd5, with White's minority attack against Black's pawn on d5.

character.notes: Queen's Gambit Declined set-up with piece trades and few forcing lines; Black is very hard to break down.

structure.notes: After the exchange on d5 there is a half-open c-file for White and a symmetrical-ish structure; semi-open.

level.notes: Some forcing lines are known, but the typical plans are easy; intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: 6.Nf3 h6 7.Bh4 b6 (Tartakower)
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 h6 7. Bh4 b6
sublines_that_differ.how: The same structure with more flexibility on the sixth move; the Neo-Orthodox name goes with this order.

character.reason: Black is hard to break down and the play is steady, with trades.

structure.reason: Exchange on d5 gives a half-open c-file and a Carlsbad-like structure.

plans.reason: White goes for the Carlsbad minority attack.
